subject: Erase policy cutover: backup pruning & TTL alignment
messages:
From: legal@pioneerhealth.com
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-contact@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2029 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Initial request — retention alignment and backup purge timing

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Pioneer Health is preparing a compliance cutover for our data-retention policy and we need to align on a few items before the July 31 production freeze: 

- Confirmation of Redwood's standard backup retention and the schedule for pruning immutable snapshots.
- How deletion requests are executed end-to-end (timeline from request -> purge) and what evidence/proof of deletion we receive.
- Log retention exceptions: our auditors require a documented exception process for activity logs older than 90 days.
- Subprocessor visibility and whether any backup copies exist outside of primary cloud storage (including restoration windows).

Attached is a short request packet showing the fields our legal/audit team needs (Pioneer_Retention_Request.pdf). Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the technical plan and whether a DPA amendment is required?

We'd like a proposed timeline and any mitigation (e.g., temporary grace windows, escrow snapshots) you can offer.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Pioneer Health — Legal Operations
[attachment: Pioneer_Retention_Request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <legal@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial request — retention alignment and backup purge timing

Maya —

Appreciate the packet and the timeline. I'm Jordan, I own commercial/contract for Pioneer and will coordinate with our infra team (Kimberly) and Data Contracts (Karthik). High-level answers up front, followed by proposed next steps: 

Summary answers:
- Backup pruning: by default Redwood retains immutable daily snapshots for 60 days for hosted customers; weekly snapshots are retained 180 days. Dedicated/private deployments can be configured per contract.
- Deletion workflow: request tracked -> data flagged for erase -> purge job scheduled -> forensic evidence export generated and delivered. Typical bulk purge completes in 48–96 hours after scheduling, depending on restore-window overlap.
- Log exceptions: we support documented exception requests with an approval path; exceptions are time-boxed and require a signed DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: our subprocessor list is published and we will confirm whether any backup caching resides with a subprocessor outside the primary storage region.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Draft a narrow DPA addendum covering the audit hold window and retention carveouts. I've attached a starter (DPA_addendum_draft.docx) — please review.
2) Kimberly to propose a technical purge schedule that meets your July 31 freeze and provides a 14-day forensic grace window.
3) We can provide a deletion evidence bundle (S3 export + checksum manifest + log extract) once purge completes.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync Monday to agree SLA and any escrow needs?

— Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_addendum_draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <legal@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2029 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial request — retention alignment and backup purge timing

Maya / Jordan —

Technical notes from infra:

- Snapshots/Backups: Redwood's snapshot tiers: hourly (48h), daily (60d), weekly (180d), monthly (optional, 2y). For hosted accounts we don't enable monthly by default; we can add it for Pioneer as a contract option.

- Purge mechanics: purge is gated by: active restores, cross-region replication, and any legal hold flags. Our purge pipeline has a two-phase process: mark-for-delete -> final-prune job. We can run final-prune during a controlled maintenance window to minimize risk.

- Proposed plan to satisfy Pioneer auditors while keeping risk low:
  * Cutover week (week of Jul 29): freeze new snapshot rolling for retention tiers you want to shorten.
  * Grace window: 14 days after freeze to capture any forensic holds. During those 14 days we keep a hold copy in a region-limited escrow bucket (read-only).
  * Final prune: after the 14-day hold window we run final-prune across targeted buckets. Expected completion: 24–72 hours depending on object counts.

- For logs older than 90d: we can implement an exceptions register. Exceptions require: request ID, owner, retention window, business justification, and signed DPA addendum. Exceptions are visible in the Console and exported in the evidence bundle.

A couple questions for Pioneer ops: do you need continuous-read access to the escrow snapshots during the 14-day hold or only post-request evidence exports?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ops-contact@pioneerhealth.com (Pioneer Health Ops)
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial request — retention alignment and backup purge timing

Jordan / Kim —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from operations: 

- Pioneer needs the ability to trigger a forensic export at any time during the 14-day grace window without additional approvals. Read-only access to escrowed snapshots would help accelerate internal triage.
- For the evidence bundle: we require an MD5/SHA256 manifest per object and a signed attestation that the objects were removed from live storage.
- On exceptions: our auditors will expect a maximum exception length of 180 days, with automatic reminders at 30/90/150 days.

Attached is our forensic requirements checklist; please mark which items Redwood can deliver (forensic_hold_checklist.xlsx).

We are comfortable proceeding if Redwood can: provide read-only escrow access during the 14-day window, generate the artifact manifest + signed attestation, and add the DPA addendum for log exceptions.

Best,
Samir Rao
Pioneer Health — Platform Ops
[attachment: forensic_hold_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <legal@pioneerhealth.com>, Samir Rao <ops-contact@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2029 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial request — retention alignment and backup purge timing

Team —

Thanks — we can commit to the following in writing: 

- Read-only escrow access during the 14-day forensic grace window (console role + temporary token).
- Evidence bundle post-prune: object manifest (SHA256) + signed attestation from Redwood infra.
- DPA addendum: we'll finalize language to cap exceptions at 180 days with automated reminders at the 30/90/150-day marks.

Action items I will own:
- Jordan: finalize DPA addendum and circulate for signature by EOD Wed (DocuSign link will be included).
- Kimberly: produce an itemized purge runbook and estimated object counts by Tue COB.
- Karthik: confirm subprocessor scope for backup caching and whether any subprocessor requires cross-border transfer notifications.

I'll set a 30-minute sync for Tue 09:00 PT to review the runbook and the addendum. Calendar invite + DocuSign link: https://calendar.redwood.com/j/retention-sync/13579 (placeholder).

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference
